Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retriever.summary: The smallest retriever, a red Canadian dog that lures ducks within range by playing at the water's edge.
funFacts: "Tolling" means luring: the dog's playful splashing draws curious ducks closer.
It's the provincial dog of Nova Scotia.

Old English Sheepdog.summary: A big, shaggy English drover's dog famous for its profuse coat and rolling, bear-like gait.
funFacts: Drovers' dogs traditionally had docked tails, which earned the breed the nickname "bobtail."
Paul McCartney's Old English Sheepdog, Martha, inspired the Beatles song "Martha My Dear."

Otterhound.summary: A large, shaggy British scent hound bred to hunt otters, now one of the world's rarest breeds.
funFacts: There are thought to be fewer than 1,000 Otterhounds in the world.
Otter hunting was banned in England in 1978, leaving the breed without its job.

Papillon.summary: A dainty toy spaniel named for its butterfly-wing ears, a favorite of European royalty for centuries.
funFacts: "Papillon" is French for butterfly.
Papillons appear in many Renaissance paintings, often on the laps of noblewomen.

Pekingese.summary: A lion-like toy breed that was once reserved for the Chinese imperial court.
funFacts: A Pekingese named Sun Yat-sen was one of three dogs to survive the sinking of the Titanic.
Legend says stealing one from the imperial palace was punishable by death.

Pembroke Welsh Corgi.summary: A short-legged Welsh cattle herder with a foxy face, famous as Queen Elizabeth II's favorite breed.
funFacts: Queen Elizabeth II owned more than 30 Pembroke Corgis during her reign.
Welsh legend says fairies rode corgis, leaving a "saddle" mark on their coats.

Petit Basset Griffon Vendeen.summary: A small, rough-coated French scent hound bred to hunt rabbits in the rugged Vendée region.
funFacts: Its name describes it: small (petit), low (basset), rough-coated (griffon), from the Vendée.
A PBGV named Buddy Holly won Best in Show at Westminster in 2023.

Pharaoh Hound.summary: An elegant rabbit-hunting hound from Malta, known for its amber eyes and glowing red coat.
funFacts: When excited, its nose and ears flush pink — it "blushes."
It's the national dog of Malta, where it's called Kelb tal-Fenek, "rabbit dog."

Plott Hound.summary: A brindle American hound descended from German boar-hunting dogs brought over by the Plott family in 1750.
funFacts: It's the state dog of North Carolina.
Unlike most American hounds, it descends from German rather than British dogs.

Pointer.summary: The classic English bird dog that freezes in a "point" to show hunters where game is hiding.
funFacts: Many Pointer puppies point instinctively at a few weeks old, with no training.
The dog in the Westminster Kennel Club's logo is a Pointer named Sensation.

Pomeranian.summary: A tiny, fluffy spitz bred down from larger sled-type dogs and made popular by Queen Victoria.
funFacts: Queen Victoria's love of small Pomeranians helped shrink the breed to its modern size.
Two Pomeranians survived the sinking of the Titanic.

Pomsky.summary: A cross between a Pomeranian and a Siberian Husky, bred to look like a miniature husky.
funFacts: Pomskies are usually bred by artificial insemination, with the Husky as the mother.
The mix shot to fame through viral photos online in the early 2010s.

Poodle.summary: A highly intelligent breed in three sizes, originally a German water retriever and now the national dog of France.
funFacts: The fancy show clip started as a practical cut to lighten the coat for swimming while keeping joints warm.
"Poodle" comes from the German "Pudel," related to splashing in water.
Poodles are widely ranked as the second most intelligent breed, after the Border Collie.

Portuguese Water Dog.summary: A curly-coated Portuguese fisherman's dog that herded fish into nets and carried messages between boats.
funFacts: Bo and Sunny, the Obama family's dogs, were Portuguese Water Dogs.
Webbed feet and a waterproof coat make them excellent swimmers.

Pug.summary: An ancient Chinese toy breed with a wrinkled face and curled tail, loved for its comedic personality.
funFacts: A Pug named Pompey is said to have saved William of Orange from assassins in 1572.
The breed's motto is "Multum in parvo" — a lot in a little.

Redbone Coonhound.summary: A sleek, solid-red American coonhound, a fast hunter in rough terrain and an easygoing family dog.
funFacts: Old Dan and Little Ann in Where the Red Fern Grows were Redbone Coonhounds.
Redbones are nimble enough to hunt in swamps and mountains alike.

Rhodesian Ridgeback.summary: A muscular African hound developed in Rhodesia (now Zimbabwe) to track lions and hold them at bay.
funFacts: The ridge along its back is hair growing in the opposite direction from the rest of the coat.
It was nicknamed the "African Lion Hound."

Rottweiler.summary: A powerful German breed descended from Roman drover dogs, used to herd cattle and pull butchers' carts in the town of Rottweil.
funFacts: Butchers in Rottweil are said to have tied money pouches to their dogs' collars to keep the money safe.
Rottweilers were among the first police dogs.

Saint Bernard.summary: A giant Alpine rescue dog bred by monks at the Great St Bernard Hospice to find travelers lost in the snow.
funFacts: A St. Bernard named Barry is credited with saving more than 40 people in the early 1800s.
The famous brandy barrel around the neck is mostly a myth, popularized by a painting.
Beethoven, star of the 1992 family movie, is a St. Bernard.

Saluki.summary: One of the oldest dog breeds, a graceful desert sighthound bred to hunt gazelles across the Middle East.
funFacts: Saluki-like dogs appear in ancient Egyptian tomb paintings.
Bedouin tribes prized Salukis so highly they called them el hor, "the noble one."

Samoyed.summary: A fluffy white Siberian spitz bred by the Samoyedic peoples to herd reindeer, pull sleds and keep them warm at night.
funFacts: The upturned corners of its mouth, the "Sammy smile," are said to keep drool from freezing into icicles.
Samoyeds pulled sleds on early polar expeditions, including Roald Amundsen's.

Schipperke.summary: A small black Belgian dog that guarded canal barges and caught rats, nicknamed the "little captain."
funFacts: Its name is Flemish for "little boatman" or "little captain."
Its ruff and tailless rear give it a distinctive fox-like silhouette.

Scottish Deerhound.summary: A tall, rough-coated Scottish sighthound bred to hunt red deer, once owned only by nobility.
funFacts: In the Middle Ages, no one below the rank of earl was allowed to own one.
A Deerhound named Hickory won Best in Show at Westminster in 2011.

Scottish Terrier.summary: A sturdy, bearded Highland terrier bred to hunt foxes and badgers, nicknamed the "Diehard."
funFacts: Franklin D. Roosevelt's Scottie, Fala, is part of his memorial in Washington, D.C.
The Scottie is one of the playing pieces in Monopoly.

Sealyham Terrier.summary: A sturdy white Welsh terrier bred to hunt otters, badgers and foxes, now a rare breed.
funFacts: Alfred Hitchcock walks his own two Sealyhams in his cameo in The Birds (1963).
It was developed by Captain John Edwardes on his Sealyham estate in the 1800s.

Shar-Pei.summary: An ancient Chinese guard dog famous for its deep wrinkles, hippo-shaped muzzle and blue-black tongue.
funFacts: In 1978 Guinness listed it as the world's rarest dog breed.
"Shar-Pei" means "sand skin," for its rough, bristly coat.

Shetland Sheepdog.summary: A small, agile herding dog from Scotland's Shetland Islands that looks like a miniature Rough Collie.
funFacts: Shelties were bred to keep sheep, ponies and birds out of crofters' gardens.
They're consistently among the top breeds in obedience and agility competitions.

Shiba Inu.summary: Japan's oldest and smallest native spitz, a bold, fox-like hunting dog with a famously independent streak.
funFacts: The "Doge" meme and the Dogecoin cryptocurrency feature a Shiba Inu named Kabosu.
Shibas are known for the "Shiba scream," a dramatic high-pitched protest.

Shih Tzu.summary: A "little lion dog" bred as a palace companion for Chinese royalty, with a flowing coat and a sweet nature.
funFacts: "Shih Tzu" means "little lion" in Mandarin.
Nearly all modern Shih Tzus descend from 14 dogs used to rebuild the breed in the 20th century.

Siberian Husky.summary: A medium-sized sled dog bred by the Chukchi people of Siberia for endurance in extreme cold.
funFacts: Huskies including Balto and Togo relayed diphtheria medicine to Nome, Alaska, in the 1925 "Great Race of Mercy."
Many Huskies have blue eyes, or one blue and one brown.

Silky Terrier.summary: A small Australian terrier with a glossy blue-and-tan coat, bred from Yorkshire and Australian Terriers.
funFacts: It's often mistaken for a Yorkie but is a bit larger, with a more wedge-shaped head.
Despite its Toy-group size, it was bred to hunt snakes and rodents.

Smooth Fox Terrier.summary: A lively, smooth-coated English terrier bred to chase foxes out of their dens during hunts.
funFacts: The AKC showed Smooth and Wire Fox Terriers as one breed until 1985.
Nipper, the dog in the "His Master's Voice" logo, is often said to have been part Smooth Fox Terrier.

Soft Coated Wheaten Terrier.summary: A cheerful Irish farm terrier with a silky, wheat-colored coat and a famously enthusiastic greeting.
funFacts: Wheatens greet people by bouncing up joyfully — fans call it the "Wheaten greetin'."
Puppies are born dark; the coat lightens to wheaten by about age two.

Staffordshire Bull Terrier.summary: A muscular, affectionate English terrier from Staffordshire, one of the UK's most popular family dogs.
funFacts: In the UK it's nicknamed the "nanny dog" for its fondness for children.
It's one of the most popular breeds in the United Kingdom.

Standard Schnauzer.summary: The original schnauzer, a bearded German farm dog that guarded property and caught vermin.
funFacts: The Miniature and Giant Schnauzers were both developed from it.
Standard Schnauzers appear in paintings by Albrecht Dürer from around 1500.

Sussex Spaniel.summary: A low, golden-liver spaniel from Sussex, bred to flush game in dense undergrowth while barking.
funFacts: Unlike most spaniels, it barks while hunting, which hunters call "giving tongue."
A Sussex named Stump won Westminster in 2009 at age 10, the oldest winner ever.

Tibetan Mastiff.summary: An ancient Himalayan guardian with a lion-like mane, bred to protect monasteries and nomads' flocks.
funFacts: A Tibetan Mastiff puppy was reportedly sold in China for about $1.5 million in 2011.
Its thick double coat lets it shrug off Himalayan winters.

Tibetan Terrier.summary: A shaggy Tibetan companion dog — not actually a terrier — kept by monks as a good-luck charm.
funFacts: Its large, flat "snowshoe" feet help it travel over snow.
Tibetans considered them bringers of luck and gave them as gifts rather than selling them.

Toy Terrier.summary: A small, sleek black-and-tan terrier, essentially a toy-sized Manchester Terrier, bred as a ratter and companion.
Toy Terrier.group: Toy variety of the Manchester Terrier
funFacts: In the U.S., it's shown as the Toy variety of the Manchester Terrier.
Its upright, candle-flame-shaped ears are a breed signature.

Treeing Walker Coonhound.summary: A fast, tricolor American coonhound descended from English Foxhounds, bred to chase raccoons up trees.
funFacts: It descends in part from a stolen dog named Tennessee Lead, bred into Walker foxhounds in the 1800s.
Coonhound fans call it "the people's choice."

Vizsla.summary: A sleek, golden-rust Hungarian pointer bred for falconry and bird hunting, famous for its affectionate nature.
funFacts: Vizslas are nicknamed "Velcro dogs" because they stick so close to their owners.
A Vizsla named Chartay was the first dog to earn AKC championships in five different sports.

Weimaraner.summary: A sleek, silver-gray German hunting dog bred by nobles of the Weimar court to hunt big game.
funFacts: Its silvery coat and light eyes earned it the nickname "Gray Ghost."
Photographer William Wegman's Weimaraners have appeared on Sesame Street.

Welsh Springer Spaniel.summary: A red-and-white Welsh gundog, a little smaller than the English Springer, bred to flush birds in rough country.
funFacts: It only comes in one color combination: red and white.
Welshies are known for the stamina to hunt all day in rugged terrain.

West Highland White Terrier.summary: A plucky white Scottish terrier bred to hunt rats, foxes and badgers among the Highland rocks.
funFacts: Legend says Colonel Edward Malcolm started breeding white terriers after mistaking his reddish terrier for a fox.
A Westie is the face of Cesar dog food.

Whippet.summary: A lightning-fast English sighthound bred by miners for racing and rabbit coursing, calm and cuddly at home.
funFacts: Whippets can reach about 35 mph and are known for incredible acceleration.
They were nicknamed "the poor man's racehorse."

Wire Fox Terrier.summary: A jaunty, wire-coated English fox terrier and the most successful breed in Westminster Best in Show history.
funFacts: Wire Fox Terriers have won Best in Show at Westminster 15 times, more than any other breed.
Snowy, Tintin's faithful companion, is a Wire Fox Terrier.
Asta in The Thin Man films was a Wire Fox Terrier.

Wirehaired Pointing Griffon.summary: A shaggy, bearded all-purpose gundog developed in the late 1800s by Dutch breeder Eduard Korthals.
funFacts: In Europe it's known as the Korthals Griffon.
Its harsh coat protects it in thick brush and cold water.

Xoloitzcuintli.summary: An ancient Mexican breed, mostly hairless, revered by the Aztecs and named after the god Xolotl.
funFacts: The Aztecs believed Xolos guided souls through the underworld.
Dante in Pixar's Coco is a Xoloitzcuintli.
It's the national dog of Mexico.

Yorkshire Terrier.summary: A tiny, glamorous terrier with a silky blue-and-tan coat, originally bred to catch rats in Yorkshire mills.
funFacts: A Yorkie named Smoky served in World War II and is considered one of the first therapy dogs.
A Yorkie's coat is closer in texture to human hair than to typical dog fur.
